Maya: RCAs are posted — summary + action checklist is here: https://go.redwood/internal/postmortems/deploy-cache-cascade-2026. Please review and add any missed follow-ups. :mag:

Maya: Short summary: a deploy that tightened cache TTLs combined with an unchecked canary ramp caused a cache-miss cascade and client-side retry amplification. This hit p95/p99 and generated customer-reported slowdowns for ~25 minutes (01:18-01:43 UTC).

Devon: Impact numbers in the doc: p99 latency jumped from ~300ms -> ~1.1s, error surface increased ~4-7% for some routes. No Golden Key access or data leak.

Priya: Root causes (high level):
- Config change reduced cache TTLs in the rollout bundle.
- Canary scheduler allowed more simultaneous canary nodes than intended during a traffic spike.
- Retry propagation from clients plus lack of router-side rate limiting amplified load.

ops-bot: [01:12] Canary rollout started: model-service v3.2.4 -> 15 canary instances. Health checks green.

Maya: Immediate mitigations applied during incident: paused rollout, reverted TTL to previous value, temporarily enabled stricter router-level retry budgets.

Ken: Proposed owners and targets in the doc:
- Mitigation 1: Add an automatic rollback guard for cache config changes (owner: @Maya) — ETA: 48h.
- Mitigation 2: Enforce max canary concurrency to 3% of pool and make it a runtime toggle (owner: @Devon) — ETA: 5 days.
- Mitigation 3: Router-level rate limiter and retry budget enforcement (owner: @Ken) — ETA: 2 weeks.
- Mitigation 4: Add KV TTL change preflight in CI that runs against a small warm pool (owner: @Priya) — ETA: 1 week.

Priya: Question: can we make the canary cap adjustable from the console or do we need a deploy?

Devon: We'll wire it as a runtime flag in the orchestrator; no deploy needed for flips after the change. I'll add a dashboard tile + alert.

Maya: Good. Also adding a tiny post-deploy smoke check to the pipeline to exercise KV behavior for 60s before allowing additional canaries.

triage-bot: [01:39] Postmortem review scheduled: Monday 10:00 PT in #postmortems. Agenda: confirm owners, review CI preflight plan, finalize customer note.

Ken: I can draft the customer-facing note for Dedicated customers if someone shares the final affected pool list and the aggregated incident metrics.

Maya: I'll attach the metrics snapshot to the doc (section 2) and tag the affected customer groups.

Devon: I'll open the PR for the canary cap and the runtime flag today. Ken, I'll throw you the telemetry snippets for the note when it's ready.

Priya: I'll add the CI preflight steps to the doc and a checklist for on-call to run once it's merged.

Maya: Thanks all. Please update the RCA doc with progress checks and mark any blockers. Link again: https://go.redwood/internal/postmortems/deploy-cache-cascade-2026 — ping me for questions or if you need access. :white_check_mark:
